title: Coach Lou's Big Pep Talk
text:
All right, team, gather around! Bring it in close.

Today is Sports Day, and I am so proud of you already. You practiced every day. You ran laps, you stretched your {plural noun}, and you learned how to {verb} like champions. Now remember what we talked about. Keep your eyes on the ball and your feet on the {noun}. If you feel nervous, take a deep breath and think about {plural noun}.

The other team is very good too. Their coach told me they eat {food} for breakfast every morning. That is fine. We have something even better. We have heart, and we have {adjective} socks. When you get out there, play {adverb}. Pass the ball, cheer for your friends, and if you hear me yell "{exclamation}!" that means run.

Win or lose, we are going out for {adjective} pizza after the game. Now put your hands in. On three, everybody shout "Go {adjective} {plural noun}!"

title: Live from the Sack Race
text:
Hello, sports fans, and welcome to the big sack race at Oak Park Elementary! I am Ted, and here with me is my partner, Jill.

Thanks, Ted. What a {adjective} day for a race. The sun is out, and the racers are climbing into their {plural noun}. The whistle blows! And they are off! Look at Mia in lane two. She is hopping {adverb}, Jill!

Yes, Ted, and look at Sam in lane three. He is not hopping at all. He is {verb ending in ing}. I have never seen that in a sack race before. The crowd is cheering. Someone in the stands is waving a giant {noun}.

Here comes the finish line! Mia {past tense verb} across first, and Sam is right behind her, still not hopping. Everyone made it! All the racers will get a {color} ribbon and a cup of {food}.

That is all from the sack race. Next up is the {adjective} relay. Do not {verb} away, folks!

title: Sports Day Schedule at Willow Creek
text:
Welcome to Sports Day at Willow Creek School! Here is the plan for today.

9:00: Opening parade. Each class will march around the field holding a sign shaped like a {noun}. The kindergarten class will lead the way, walking very {adverb}. 9:30: Warm-ups with Coach Bea. We will touch our toes, shake our {plural noun}, and do {number} jumping jacks. 10:00: The three-legged race. Partners will tie their legs together and try to {verb} to the finish line.

10:45: Water break. Please drink lots of water. Lemonade and {adjective} orange slices will be on the snack table. 11:00: The water balloon toss. Last year, Mr. Grant's balloon {past tense verb} right on his hat, and he laughed for ten minutes. 11:30: Parents and teachers tug-of-war. The teachers have been practicing by pulling {plural noun} across the gym.

12:00: Picnic lunch on the grass. Bring a blanket and a {adjective} hat. 12:30: Everyone gets a medal for {verb ending in ing}!

title: Official Rules of the Egg and Spoon Race
text:
Welcome to the egg and spoon race! Please read these rules before you begin.

Rule one: Each racer gets one spoon and one egg. The eggs have been boiled, so they will not make a mess. You may give your egg a name, like Eggbert or {silly word}. Rule two: Hold the spoon in your hand, not in your mouth. You may hold it {adverb}, but you may not use glue, tape, or {plural noun}. Rule three: When Ms. Park blows the whistle, walk to the big {adjective} cone and back. You may not run. You may not {verb}. You may only walk.

Rule four: If your egg falls, that is okay! Pick it up, put it back on your spoon, and keep {verb ending in ing}. Rule five: Cheer for every egg. A good cheer sounds like this: "Go, egg, go! You are a {adjective} {noun}!"

Rule six: Every racer gets a sticker and a {noun}. The eggs will go home and become {food} sandwiches. Have fun, and remember, the most important thing is to be {adjective}.

title: Dear Diary, Field Day Was Great
text:
Dear Diary,

Today was Field Day, and it was the best day of the whole year. I wore my team shirt, which is bright {color} and has a {noun} on the front. The first event was the hula hoop contest. I kept my hoop spinning for {number} seconds. My friend Leo kept his hoop going while he {past tense verb} at the same time. Everybody clapped.

Next was the obstacle course. We had to crawl under a net, hop through tires, and {verb} over a pile of {plural noun}. I went {adverb} and made it to the end. At lunch, my mom brought a cooler full of {adjective} snacks. We ate on the grass and watched the teachers race. Mr. Kim ran so fast his whistle started {verb ending in ing}.

At the end of the day, everyone got a ribbon. Mine says "Most {adjective} Hopper." I am going to hang it above my bed next to my {noun}.

title: How to Do the Blue Team Cheer
text:
Welcome to the Blue Team! Every team needs a great cheer, and ours is the best. Here is how to do it.

Step one: Stand in a line with your teammates. Put your hands on your hips and look very {adjective}. Step two: Stomp your feet {number} times. Stomp loudly, like a herd of {plural noun}. Step three: Clap your hands over your head and shout, "We are Blue, we are true, we can {verb} and so can you!"

Step four: Spin around once. If you get dizzy, that is okay. Just hold on to your {noun} and wait. Step five: Wiggle your {body part} and say "{silly word}" as {adverb} as you can. Step six: Jump up high and pretend you are a {adjective} rocket. Step seven: Give a high five to the person next to you and say, "Nice {verb ending in ing}!"

Coach Mae says if we do our cheer every morning, we will feel {adjective} all day long.

title: The Sports Day Awards
text:
Good afternoon, families! Thank you for coming to the Sports Day Awards. Every student worked hard today, so every student gets an award.

The Super Sprinter Award goes to Jada, who ran so {adverb} that her shoelaces came untied. The Best Teammate Award goes to Marco, who cheered for everyone and shared his {plural noun} with the whole class. The Golden Spoon Award goes to Ellie. She carried her egg all the way to the finish line on a {noun}.

The Big Jump Award goes to Omar. He jumped {number} feet and landed like a {adjective} {animal}. The Sunshine Award goes to Ms. Wu, who stood at the finish line all day {verb ending in ing}. The Silly Hat Award goes to Principal Green. His hat had {plural noun} glued all over it, and it {past tense verb} every time he moved.

Thank you all for a {adjective} day. Next year, we will add a new event: the {adjective} {noun} relay. Please practice at home!

title: Snack Table Sign-Up Sheet
text:
Hello, Sports Day families! We need your help with the snack table. Please write your name next to one item and bring it on Friday morning.

Water bottles: Please bring {number} bottles. Athletes get very thirsty after {verb ending in ing} all morning. Orange slices: Cut into small pieces. Coach Dan likes them {adjective} and cold. Granola bars: Any kind is fine, as long as there are no {plural noun} inside. Sunscreen: Please bring a big bottle. Mr. Tate puts it on his nose, his ears, and his {body part}.

Napkins: We need lots of napkins. The kindergarten class likes to {verb} with them. Fruit cups: Last year someone brought a fruit cup shaped like a {noun}, and it was a big hit. Extra treat: One lucky family can bring a {adjective} surprise. Last year it was a giant bowl of {food}, and the students {past tense verb} with joy.

Thank you so much! The snack table is the most {adjective} part of the day.

title: Please Pick Me for Team Mascot
text:
Dear Coach Rivera,

My name is Nora, and I would like to be the mascot for the Green Team on Sports Day. I would be a great mascot because I am very {adjective}. I can cheer loudly, dance {adverb}, and do a cartwheel almost every time.

I already have a costume. It is a giant {animal} suit that my grandma made. It has a long tail and {number} fuzzy {plural noun} on the back. It is a little bit smelly, but only on hot days.

As the mascot, I will run up and down the field and help the team {verb}. When our team scores, I will do my special dance, called the {silly word}. When the other team scores, I will clap for them too, because that is good manners. I have also been practicing my mascot noises. My best one sounds like a {noun} {verb ending in ing}.

I promise to be {adjective} and to never take off my {noun} during the game.

Your friend,
Nora

title: Tug-of-War Ends in a Tie
text:
Good evening. This is Ruby Wells with the Sports Day news.

Today at Elm Street School, the big tug-of-war between the Red Team and the Yellow Team ended in a tie for the first time in {number} years. The match began at two o'clock. Both teams grabbed the rope and pulled {adverb}. The crowd cheered so loudly that a {noun} fell off the bleachers.

For ten whole minutes, nobody moved. The Red Team pulled. The Yellow Team pulled. A {adjective} squirrel sat in the middle of the field and watched. Then something surprising happened. Both teams started {verb ending in ing} at the same time. They laughed so hard that they all sat down on the grass.

The referee, Mr. Ito, {past tense verb} and blew his whistle. He said it was the most {adjective} match he had ever seen. After the game, both teams shared a big bowl of {plural noun} and promised to {verb} again next year.

Reporting live from the field, this is Ruby Wells. Back to you, {name}.
